report.summary: During the requested query interval, checkout-service resident memory rose 1.8x, from 687.64MiB to 1220.35MiB. Logs also show heap usage at 92% with GC overhead approaching, followed by repeated Java heap-space OutOfMemoryErrors. These findings support substantial heap pressure, but do not identify its underlying mechanism or establish exact onset or continuous behavior across the interval.

likely_causes.title: Excessive heap retention or allocation in checkout-service
likely_causes.rationale: The memory increase together with repeated high-heap/GC-overhead warnings and Java heap-space errors supports excessive heap pressure. The evidence does not distinguish a memory leak from high allocation, workload-specific retention, or another heap-consuming behavior.

supporting_evidence.detail: Threshold-validated resident memory for checkout-service rose 1.8x, from 687.64MiB to 1220.35MiB (anomaly_detected=True).
17 sampled WARN occurrences of `GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92%` (version=v1.4.2; sample timestamps 2026-10-26T11:48:32+00:00 to 2026-10-26T13:04:32+00:00).
Five sampled ERROR occurrences of `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` (version=v1.4.2; sample timestamps 2026-10-26T12:42:32+00:00 to 2026-10-26T13:04:32+00:00).

next_steps: Capture and analyze a heap dump or allocation profile to identify dominant retained objects and allocation sources.
Review JVM heap and garbage-collection telemetry, including post-GC live-set size, allocation rate, and configured heap limits.
Correlate memory behavior with request rate and workload mix; no request-rate evidence was provided, so increased traffic cannot be concluded.
Check whether the memory trend and log samples are continuous and determine the incident onset; aggregate trends and sample timestamps do not establish exact timing or causal ordering.
